support.title: Capitalism, but make it tropical
support.intro1: Yes, açaí — the purple gold of Pará that foreigners discovered yesterday and now sell as exotic. I chose it over "buy me a coffee" because at least nobody pretends it's a cheap knock-off (perhaps tacky, who knows).
support.intro2: I'm Brazilian (unfortunately). Translation: I write code in a currency that devalues if you breathe, in a country where politicians treat public funds like pocket money, in an economy held together with duct tape and collective denial. I don't code for fun (sometimes I do) — it's what pays my bills.
support.intro3: If my work ever saved you time, a bug, or a therapy session, feel free to send crypto below. No pressure — unlike literally everything else in adult life.
support.bitcoinDesc: Good old BTC. One of the last ways to move value without asking a bank for permission — those lovely institutions run by people who'd sell their own children for another zero on the balance sheet.
support.ethereumDesc: Ethereum: opened the door to a thousand "revolutionary" apps that mostly revolutionised how fast you can lose money. Still beats watching your money rot in a savings account, though.
